# R753 — No one-edge equivariant selector; minimal three-PASS cyclic BRC ledger

Status: AUTHOR-PROVED FINITE COMBINATORIAL RESULT / CANDIDATE V29 PORT BRIDGE / NOT NATIVE TRIADIC_CLOSURE_E / NOT FOUNDATION
Researcher lineage: EM-X6-0E46B2; task RS-X6-TRIADIC-CLOSURE-DYNAMICS; Activity RA-98CE0270814B2431AD745438; prior Run RUN-14a5d6f361d4bb24a99a717a (native resume outcome must be checked independently).
Frozen task science: awdawmip/enterprise-math@a72226e2430ffa4786321ac86e7f0c599d5f0389; source taskbook awdawmip/enterprise-math@12b4fb233a8feddc288616595f4311dd67e93a06:research_tasks/RS_X6_TRIADIC_CLOSURE_DYNAMICS_20260906.md.
Precisely used candidate inputs: R751/R752 author source awdawmip/enterprise-math@10d7da2034f717885fdfe096e2e0d8ad17159883; V29 observed source at deb8bbbf9d844c0ceb777631e576763a634eed99:research_notes/X6_NETWORK_EVENT_LEDGER_AND_CONTRAST_TRANSDUCER_V29_20260906.md; V39 scope at same source:research_notes/X6_CYCLE_CURRENT_S3_OPERATION_SAFE_PORT_V39_20260906.md.
This analysis does not repin the frozen scientific inputs; newer candidates are comparison subjects.

## Exact question
R752B chooses one V29 PASS from an *unmarked oriented* signed triad by marking the smallest numbered axis. Does this selector preserve the established axis-permutation skeleton S6? If it does not, what is the smallest nonnegative V29 PASS ledger supported on the three cyclic Port transitions that is both mark-independent and S6-equivariant?

## Finite carrier and typed BRC pushforward
Let P={ (i,s) : 0<=i<6, s in {-1,+1} } be a DECLARED local Port alphabet at one Cell c, distinct from an admitted force-to-Link embedding. Let X be the set of cyclic rotation classes [p,q,r] with pairwise distinct native axes and each signed source p=(i,s), etc. Reversed cyclic order is a different state; cyclic changes of the starting mark are not. Thus |X|=C(6,3)*2^3*2=320.

The S6 action permutes axis labels and does not change their signs or the position of a signed branch inside its cyclic order. It is the frozen finite positive-axis permutation skeleton, not the full rotation group.

The free positive BRC branch-occurrence monoid on directed signed Port pairs is N_0^{P x P}. For x=[p,q,r], define the unmarked ordered-edge occurrence family
  E(x)={(p,q),(q,r),(r,p)}
with each occurrence retained as an individual sourced branch before its pushforward to a nonnegative V29 ledger. Define
  B(x)=E_{p,q}+E_{q,r}+E_{r,p} in N_0^{P x P}.
This has three distinct nonzero entries, coefficient +1. These are three legal *individual V29 PASS count operations* PASS(c;p->q), PASS(c;q->r), PASS(c;r->p), at the declared Port alphabet. Their joint execution as a physical primitive force event is NOT assumed.

## Theorem 1 — exact S6 no-go for a single PASS edge selector
There is no S6-equivariant function f:X -> P x P such that f(x) is one of the three directed cyclic edges in E(x) for every x. In particular the R752B minimum-axis-mark rule is not S6-equivariant.

Proof. Choose x=[(+0),(+1),(+2)]. The 3-cycle g=(0 1 2) in S6 fixes x as a cyclic class, while it rotates the three edges (+0)->(+1), (+1)->(+2), (+2)->(+0) freely. Equivariance would imply f(x)=f(gx)=g f(x), impossible since none of those edges is g-fixed. For the minimum-axis selector, take x=(+0,+1,+2) and g transposing axes 0 and 1. Then g f(x)=(+1)->(+0), but f(gx)=(+0)->(+2), an explicit failure.

The obstruction is to an everywhere-defined one-edge selector, not to observing or retaining the entire cyclic source relation. No S6 group average, tie breaker or hidden ordered mark has been secretly declared primitive.

## Theorem 2 — minimal nontrivial positive equivariant cycle-supported V29 ledger
For any S6-equivariant map A:X->N_0^{P x P} whose support is included in E(x) and for which A(x) is nonzero at every x, a universal constant total PASS count m=sum_{a,b} A(x)[a,b] must satisfy m>=3 if m is independent of x. The B above attains m=3. More strongly, at every all-positive or all-negative x, its three edge multiplicities must be equal. If A(x) is required to use every cyclic edge with positive multiplicity for all x, m>=3 pointwise, with B the unique m=3 solution.

Proof. At x=[+0,+1,+2], the cyclic stabilizer C3 acts transitively on E(x). Equivariance forces the three nonnegative integer multiplicities to be equal k. Nonzero forces k>=1 and m=3k>=3. B plainly has one unit on each edge, is independent of cyclic starting mark, and for every g in S6 satisfies B(gx)=g B(x) g^{-1} (coordinate relabeling), proving existence and sharpness. Under full-support positivity the same count argument gives one on each edge at total three, hence uniqueness. Nonzero-at-every-state is part of the statement: the zero ledger is equivariant but is not a nontrivial event.

## Theorem 3 — exact V29 readouts, complete finite observation and residual
Starting from the zero V29 count ledger at Cell c, execute the three B(x) PASS occurrences. Their increments are
  Delta M=B(x);
  Delta Omega=B(x)-B(x)^T;
  Delta u=B(x)1-B(x)^T1=0.
Every Port has one incoming and one outgoing count in this directed three-cycle; hence both the local scalar sum and V29 network Q remain unchanged. This does not mean that an underlying force sum vanishes or a native TRIADIC_CLOSURE_E is validated.

The map x -> B(x) is injective on all 320 states: its three directed edges reconstruct exactly the signed cyclic Port sequence up to cyclic start. In fact Delta Omega alone is injective on X because all three positive directed edges and their reverse negatives recover the same oriented 3-cycle. Thus this declared signed-Port ledger preserves orientation and global source signs although the contrast u alone is identically zero for all 320.

In particular the 160 R751 global-sign-twin pairs have identical second-order exterior S (R752 proved their cubic split), but disjoint signed-Port supports under B, so the complete (M,Omega) V29 observation distinguishes every twin. This is a precise witness that conserving u is compatible with nonzero provenance-sensitive residual; it is not a physical third-force cancellation claim.

## Proof scope and missing native bridge
The three individual PASS increments are valid in V29's declared finite-local-Port count grammar; the composition has no extra event-level permission or V39 frame update supplied by V29. The R752B minimum-axis one-PASS convention was only a declared scheduler; it is unsuitable if exact S6 covariance is required. The B construction repairs the permutation/marking defect on the *candidate* algebraic bridge, not the missing physical Cell/Link/Port incidence.

V39 defines h in S3 only for admitted based-loop packets and states h(gamma;r)=h(r) o h(gamma). It does not license assigning a V39 holonomy to every three-PASS batch. No native legal TRIADIC_CLOSURE_E scheduler, frame coupling, force-interaction permission or general physical dynamics follows from these three theorems.

## Reproduction
Run the accompanying exact standard-library checker R753_X6_TRIADIC_PASS_COVARIANCE_CHECK.py. It enumerates all 320 cyclic signed triads, all 720 axis permutations for 230400 equivariance comparisons, checks 320 distinct B signatures and 160 global-sign-twin separations, and explicitly checks the minimum-axis counterexample. All matrices are sparse nonnegative integer ledgers; no classical propagator, trigonometry, Pi, Taylor or floating-point approximation is used. The BRC carrier is the three source-identified cyclic edge occurrences and the observer is their exact positive-integer incidence histogram. JSON evidence supplies the observed finite counts.

## Next discriminating problem
Extract an *actually admitted* X6 triadic force incidence predicate and actual native event scheduler (if any) plus the genuine V39 active-frame action on the same event. Test whether three symmetric PASS occurrences correspond to one physical event, three serial events, or none. If legal, test the induced signed BRC observer equivalence against that event; if not, isolate the missing primitive typed rule and provide a minimal model extension without claiming Foundation authority.
